title: Corrosion-Resistant Splice Straps at the Cabin Seat Track Joints, Stations 41 to 48
abstract: The seat track splice straps between stations 41 and 48 are changed to a corrosion-resistant alloy with a sealed faying surface, following galley and lavatory spillage findings on aircraft operating in humid networks.

sections.reason: Heavy maintenance findings from twenty-two aircraft returning for their first six-year check showed pitting corrosion on the seat track splice straps in the bays adjacent to the mid galley and the mid lavatory. Sixteen of the twenty-two required strap replacement and four needed a local seat track repair. All affected aircraft were operated in tropical or coastal networks. Spillage through the floor panel joints, rather than condensation, was identified as the driver by the metallurgical report.
sections.description: The splice straps D5350129600648 at each seat track joint between stations 41 and 48 are replaced by items in a corrosion-resistant alloy with a chromate-free primer and a sealed faying surface. The forward attachment lug D5350123241140 is retained but is re-shimmed to take up the small thickness difference. Clevis pins LN666073-13 and cushioned clamps EN220364-30 in the same bays are renewed as a matter of course because they are disturbed by the work. Wet assembly with sealant is mandatory at every faying surface, which is the real content of the change. Layout and installation detail are on drawings D53501230076 and D53501271738. Access is from the cabin in zones 241 and 251 with seats and floor panels removed locally.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.7 kg per aircraft. No electrical load change. Interchangeable in both directions, so a mixed installation is acceptable and an operator may replace straps bay by bay as findings arise. The corrosion inspection of the mid cabin floor moves from the six-year to the twelve-year check, which is the main maintenance benefit. The seat track inspection task requires reissue to reflect the new sealing standard and the revised interval.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00341 in July 2021. Retrofit through Service Bulletin MRD-53-1041 is normally done during a cabin reconfiguration when the floor is already open; done on its own it is a two-shift job for four people and is not economic outside a heavy check.

type_data.balance_impact: Negligible, distributed across the mid cabin
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00341, no change to the floor grid build sequence
